Bacterial Leaf Blight.cause: Bacterial infection (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) spread through water, rain splash, and infected seeds.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected debris. Avoid flood irrigation. Use disease-free seeds. Apply neem-based solutions.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.chemical_treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride (3g/L) or Streptomycin Sulphate (500ppm) at early infection. Repeat after 10 days.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.precautions: Do not apply nitrogen fertilizer during outbreak. Use resistant varieties like Pusa Basmati 1.

Bacterial Leaf Streak.cause: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola; favored by humid weather and water-splashing.
Bacterial Leaf Streak.organic_treatment: Use disease-free seeds. Avoid excessive nitrogen. Remove and burn infected material.
Bacterial Leaf Streak.chemical_treatment: Copper Hydroxide (2g/L). Streptomycin (100ppm) as seed treatment.

Bacterial Panicle Blight.cause: Burkholderia glumae; thrives in hot and humid weather during flowering.
Bacterial Panicle Blight.organic_treatment: Use certified seeds. Reduce plant density for better air circulation. Drain standing water.
Bacterial Panicle Blight.chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Streptomycin Sulphate. Spray Kasugamycin (1.5ml/L) at early boot stage.
Bacterial Panicle Blight.precautions: Rog infected panicles before seed shed. Consult KVK for severe outbreaks.

Blast.cause: Fungal infection by Magnaporthe oryzae; favored by cool nights, high humidity, and excess nitrogen.
Blast.organic_treatment: Use blast-resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen. Maintain proper spacing. Silicon-based amendments improve resistance.
Blast.chemical_treatment: Spray Tricyclazole (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane (1.5ml/L) at first sign. For neck blast, spray at booting stage. Repeat after 14 days.
Blast.precautions: Do not apply nitrogen fertilizer during blast period. Drain water at night for 3–4 days.

Brown Spot.cause: Fungal infection by Bipolaris oryzae; worsened by potassium deficiency and drought stress.
Brown Spot.organic_treatment: Apply potassium-rich compost. Maintain proper soil moisture. Use disease-free seeds treated with hot water (52°C for 10 min).
Brown Spot.chemical_treatment: Spray Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Propiconazole (1ml/L) at early infection. Repeat after 14 days.
Brown Spot.precautions: Test soil for potassium deficiency. Apply MOP (Muriate of Potash) as corrective measure.

Dead Heart.cause: Insect pest — stem borer larvae (e.g. Scirpophaga incertulas, yellow stem borer) tunnel into the stem during the vegetative stage, killing the central shoot.
Dead Heart.organic_treatment: Collect and destroy egg masses and affected tillers. Light traps for adult moths. Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids. Neem oil (3ml/L) at egg hatching.
Dead Heart.chemical_treatment: Carbofuran 3G (33kg/ha) at transplanting/early tillering. Spray Chlorantraniliprole (0.4ml/L) or Cartap Hydrochloride (2g/L) for active infestation.
Dead Heart.precautions: Avoid close plant spacing and excess nitrogen. Synchronised planting with neighbouring fields reduces overall pest pressure.

Downy Mildew.cause: Oomycete pathogen; favored by cool, wet, and cloudy conditions.
Downy Mildew.organic_treatment: Improve field drainage. Increase plant spacing. Remove infected material. Compost tea spray.
Downy Mildew.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2g/L) spray. Seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35 SD (6g/kg seed).
Downy Mildew.precautions: Avoid overhead irrigation. Ensure good airflow between rows.

Hispa.cause: Insect pest — Dicladispa armigera beetle; larvae mine leaves, adults scrape chlorophyll.
Hispa.organic_treatment: Clip and burn affected leaves. Release parasitoids. Apply neem seed kernel extract (5% NSKE). Light traps for adults.
Hispa.chemical_treatment: Spray Chlorpyrifos (2ml/L) or Quinalphos (2ml/L). Phorate granules (10G) at 10kg/ha in soil.
Hispa.precautions: Avoid excessive nitrogen. Plant at lower densities.

Tungro.cause: Viral disease transmitted by green leafhopper; causes stunted plants with yellow-orange leaf discoloration.
Tungro.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Control leafhopper vector with sticky yellow traps and neem spray.
Tungro.chemical_treatment: No direct cure. Control leafhopper vector: spray Imidacloprid (0.5ml/L) or Thiamethoxam (0.25g/L) at seedling and early tillering.
Tungro.precautions: Use tungro-resistant varieties (IR36, IR64). Avoid late planting. This is a serious disease — consult your KVK.

Normal.organic_treatment: Continue good agronomic practices: balanced fertilization, proper irrigation, and regular scouting.
Normal.precautions: Keep monitoring regularly. Preventive measures include crop rotation and certified seeds.
